text:
Yegor Sharangovich is having a season the numbers like more than the eye test does. CBS Sports wrote this week that he is still struggling to take the next step, and he told The Hockey News, "I still need to work harder." But he has five goals and 11 points in 24 games, including a power-play goal against Chicago on Saturday, and Calgary has scored about 6.4 fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice. That usually swings back.

He is not a play driver. The Flames take 47% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), close to their level without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits his puck work: 71% of his exits leave the zone with possession. He has scored in bunches for Calgary before, so the finish is in there. Our range has him around 18 goals.
